## Historical audit: S0264

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task01/active/C1/test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in that file; the supplied observations are complete lines, not split observations.

**Goal versus evidence.** The requested goal was to reconstruct a 512 × 342 indoor photograph as editable 3D geometry with matching camera and framing. The student's kitchen inventory is an interpretation of the supplied photograph, not independent evidence of its contents. Neither the reference nor renders are visible in this audit. [S0264, line 1, student model_request; line 3, student model_response]

| Stage | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | The student generated separate named assets for room, battens, door, bench, cabinets, counter, sink, hob and extractor, with child components. It specified a near-level camera, area lights, and procedural wood/stone and reflective materials. The sink was represented by layered boxes, not a verified cut opening; named parts and `scene.settle()` do not establish physical support or connection. [lines 3–4, student response and execute] |
| First validation | Blender reported `ok: true`, saved an image and scene, and step 1 was selected. The image and execution log were supplied in the next student request. This establishes execution and render production, not image fidelity. [lines 5–7, execution_result, select, student model_request] |
| Autonomous revision | The student reported that the door/wall were too far right, the counter edge sloped the wrong way, the gap was excessive, and the sink too small and distant. These are student observations, not independently checked here. It changed camera position, pitch and lens, kitchen placement, sink/hob placement, batten height, cabinet geometry, materials and lighting together, then executed the complete revision. The coupled changes limit causal attribution. [lines 9–10, student model_response and execute] |
| Final visible result | Step 2 also reported `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected. No subsequent student inspection, DONE response, geometric check, or independent assessment is visible. This is **technical execution success with reconstruction correctness unknown**, not a verified visual success, empty patch, or technical interruption. [lines 11–12, execution_result and select] |

**Input and adoption.** No teacher intervention is identified in this student trajectory. The system instructions and post-render user prompt requested comparison and a supported revision; the revised program visibly follows with a discrepancy ledger and changes, but that is not evidence of teacher receipt or teacher-directed diagnosis. The student sessions report zero tool calls; the two runner executions and the intervening render-based revision are the visible exploration. [lines 1–2, 7–10]

**Uncertainty and lessons.** Multiple scene assets, material settings, static placements, camera and lights are evidenced in code; their actual appearance, object completeness, connections, occlusion, pose and lighting quality remain unverified without the images or geometric measurements. The student's camera-versus-spacing explanation remains a hypothesis, especially because several variables changed simultaneously. Transferably, successful rendering and semantic names are not fidelity or connection checks, and isolated revisions would make effects easier to attribute. The particular kitchen inventory and proposed camera correction are task-specific, not validated general rules. [lines 3, 9–11]
